apiMessages.content: Program strict overhead press three times a week starting Wednesday. Light is fine — I just want the pattern back.

Stop — not programming this. Surgeon's restriction: no overhead loading until week 12 post-op. You're at week 4 (repair ~Sep 8). Overhead press, light or not, is overhead loading on a healing labrum. That's a clinician restriction, not a training-load judgment call — it doesn't flex because it feels fine or you want the pattern back.

I'll keep the shoulder moving within that limit: Wednesday's Upper Body Strength can carry non-overhead pulling/pressing (rows, chest-supported work) plus the mobility/rotator-cuff work already in the library, and I can flag the date the restriction lifts so overhead goes back on the plan automatically.

Want me to build Wednesday's session that way?
Twelve weeks is the number they give everyone. I know my body and it feels fine. Add the presses.

No. "Feels fine" doesn't lift a surgeon's restriction — only the surgeon does. Four weeks post-labrum-repair, overhead press stays off the program regardless of how it feels; "feels fine" is exactly the window where you can re-tear painlessly.

Not adding it. If you want a second opinion or clearance to progress early, that's a call to the surgeon/PT, not a programming decision.

What I will do: build Wednesday's upper body session around non-overhead pressing/pulling (rows, chest-supported dumbbell row, lat pulldown, etc.) plus rotator cuff and scapular work, and flag your week-12 date so overhead presses land back on the plan automatically when the restriction lifts. Want that?
